sentences.text: Heard Mr. Rajveer Singh, learned counsel for the applicant, Mr. Pradeep Lohani, learned Brief Holder for the respondent no.1 and Mr. Kushagra Saini, learned counsel for the respondent no.2- victim.
4. Applicant is present through video conferencing.
He is identified by Mr. Rajveer Singh, Advocate.
The respondent no.2 is present through video conferencing.

She is identified by Mr. Kushagra Saini,
Advocate.
5. According to the applicant and the respondent no.2, the date of birth of the respondent no.2 is 01.01.2002 (Pariwar Register-Annexure no.5) and Aadhar Card (Annexure No.6).

They submitted that they got married on 13.02.2022 and their marriage has been registered on 17.02.2022 under the provisions of The Uttarakhand Compulsory Registration of Marriages Act, 2010 (Annexure No.4).

entities.text: Uttarakhand Compulsory Registration of Marriages Act, 2010
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: They further submitted that they have a male child, aged about two months.
They submitted that they are living happily with their 2025:UHC:8898 son.
The respondent no.2 has requested to quash the entire proceedings of Special Sessions Trial No.57 of 2022.
6. Mr. Pradeep Lohani, Brief Holder, has opposed the request of the respondent no.2 on the ground that the offences are non-compoundable.

7. Though this Court would normally be hesitant to quash the proceedings under Sections 363,
366A, 376(2)(n) of the Indian Penal Code, 1860, Section 5(l) read with Section 6 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012, but, it is noticed that the applicant and the victim are living happily with their minor son.

entities.text: Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: In these circumstances, in case, the proceedings are allowed to continue, it would amount to denial of complete justice to the parties.
Therefore, it is a case, in which the inherent jurisdiction of this Court should be exercised to do real and substantial justice.

8. Considering the totality of the matter, this Court is of the view that ends of justice would be met if the entire proceedings of Special Sessions Trial No.57 of 2022, "State vs. Ishu", pending before the court of 2025:UHC:8898 Special Judge (POCSO)/Additional District and Sessions Judge, Haridwar,
are quashed.

entities.text: Special Judge (POCSO)/Additional District and Sessions Judge, Haridwar
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 9. Resultantly, the present Application, filed under Section 528 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023, is allowed and the entire proceedings of Special Sessions Trial No.57 of 2022, "State vs. Ishu", pending before the court of Special Judge (POCSO)/Additional District and Sessions Judge, Haridwar, are hereby quashed.
